newsitem.title: USA: Borden Foods plans to sell Cracker Jack, others.
newsitem.headline: Borden Foods plans to sell Cracker Jack, others.

text.p: Borden Foods Corp said this week it plans to sell several non-core product lines including Cracker Jack candy-coated popcorn and ReaLemon and ReaLime reconstituted juice in order to focus on its core pasta and related businesses.
Borden Foods is one of 10 independent operating companies created under the Borden Inc umbrella after the Columbus, Ohio-based company was taken private by investors Kohlberg Kravis Roberts in 1995.
Other units, unaffected by the Borden Foods unit's strategic plan, include gluemaker Elmer's Products Inc, snackmaker Wise Foods and Borden/Meadow Gold Dairies, home of Elsie, the Borden Cow.

When Borden Inc was a publicly traded company, it had sought to sell its dairies, but new management "took another look and retrenched" that business, focusing on its strongest geographic regions west of the Mississippi River, spokesman Nick Iammartino said in a telephone interview Thursday.
The Borden Foods unit in a statement this week said it is beginning to implement a strategy sharpening its focus on what it termed "grain-based meal solutions."
Creamettes, Prince, Catelli, Merlino's and R-F pasta brands, Classico premium pastas and sauces and Wyler's bouillon and dry soup mixes will be retained, Iammartino said.
"Using innovation to create value-added products ... is a key part of our strategy going forward," he said, adding the unit will also seek acquisitions in its focus area.

Other non-core lines that will go on the block are Eagle Brand Sweetened Condensed Milk, Creamora non-dairy coffee creamer, Kava acid-reduced instant coffee, Nonesuch mincemeat and Borden's cheese business, Iammartino said.
